title: Quality score
intro: How close every file comes to the best release your quality profiles allow, and what is missing on the way.
scanningAgain: Checking again in the background. The numbers below were checked {{when}}.
noneBody: Add Sonarr (v4 or later) or Radarr in the settings. Wardarr then checks every file against your quality profiles.
firstTitle: Checking your library for the first time
firstBody: Wardarr reads every file with its custom formats. A big library takes a few minutes; this page fills in by itself.
emptyBody: None of the quality profiles give custom formats a positive score, so there is no perfect file to measure against. Score custom formats in Sonarr or Radarr and check again.
unsupported: {{name}} {{version}} has no custom format scores. Sonarr 4 or later is needed.

error.timeout: it took too long to answer

hero.label: Library score
hero.sentence: Your library reaches {{percent}} % of the perfect score. {{perfect}} of {{files}} files are perfect.
hero.sentenceAllPerfect: Every one of your {{files}} files is perfect. Nothing left to upgrade.
hero.gap: On average a file has {{score}} of {{perfect}} points and misses {{gap}}.
hero.tiersHint: Click a state to list its files.

histogram.title: Distance to perfect
histogram.label: Files by share of the perfect score

points.title: Where the points go
points.byKindLabel: Missing points per kind of custom format
points.nothing: Nothing is missing. Every file has everything its profile asks for.
points.explain: The perfect file has the best format of each kind together. Formats of one kind (say Dolby Vision and HDR10) only count together when one of your files already has them together. Repack and proper are a bonus, never required.

files.title: Files by state
files.intro: Worst first, with what each file is missing.

search.title: Search for better releases
search.body_one: Wardarr asks Sonarr and Radarr to search for a better release of the lowest-rated files. Only files below their upgrade target count, because the apps would not replace the others. Right now that is 1 file.
search.body_other: Wardarr asks Sonarr and Radarr to search for a better release of the lowest-rated files. Only files below their upgrade target count, because the apps would not replace the others. Right now that is {{formatted}} files.
search.nothing: No file is below its upgrade target, so there is nothing to search.
search.started: Search started: {{parts}}. Sonarr and Radarr grab a better release when they find one.
search.confirmBody_one: Sonarr or Radarr searches for a better release of the lowest-rated file below its upgrade target. Every search uses API calls at your indexers.
search.confirmBody_other: Sonarr and Radarr search for a better release of the {{formatted}} lowest-rated files below their upgrade target. Every search uses API calls at your indexers.
